meta.topic: How password managers actually keep your secrets safe
meta.onePayoff: Your master password never leaves your device; only encrypted gibberish travels to the cloud.
meta.openLoop: If the company gets hacked, why don't thieves get your passwords?
meta.analogy: A digital safe deposit box where you hold the only key.

beats.narration: One breach exposes every account you own. Unless you use this.
Your data is encrypted locally before it ever touches the internet.
Old way: plain text on servers. New way: scrambled data only you can read.
Enter master password. Derive key. Decrypt vault. Access granted.
Zero-knowledge means the provider literally cannot see your secrets.
Myth: They store your master password. Fact: It never leaves your device.
Local encryption. Zero-knowledge servers. You hold the only key.
